description: NaBa(PO₂NH)₃ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2/m space group. Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.34-2.75 Å. Ba is bonded in a 9-coordinate geometry to one N and eight O atoms. The Ba-N bond length is 3.23 Å. There are a spread of Ba-O bond distances ranging from 2.67-3.05 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to two N and two O atoms to form corner-sharing PN₂O₂ tetrahedra. There is one shorter (1.68 Å) and one longer (1.71 Å) P-N bond length. There is one shorter (1.51 Å) and one longer (1.52 Å) P-O bond length. In the second P site, P is bonded to two equivalent N and two O atoms to form corner-sharing PN₂O₂ tetrahedra. Both P-N bond lengths are 1.68 Å. Both P-O bond lengths are 1.52 Å. There are two inequivalent N sites. In the first N site, N is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to two P and one H atom. The N-H bond length is 1.03 Å. In the second N site, N is bonded in a distorted trigonal non-coplanar geometry to one Ba, two equivalent P, and one H atom. The N-H bond length is 1.03 Å. There are two inequivalent H sites. In the first H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one N atom. In the second H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one N atom. There are four inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted single-bond geometry to one Na, one Ba, and one P atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, two equivalent Ba, and one P atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted single-bond geometry to two equivalent Ba and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted single-bond geometry to two equivalent Na and one P atom.
